newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees first half 1997 inflation at 26 pct.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees first half 1997 inflation at 26 pct.

text.p: Turkish Finance Minister Abdullatif Sener said on Friday the government estimated the inflation rate in the first six month of 1997 would be 26 percent.
This compares with 43.7 percent for wholesale inflation and 36.7 percent of consumer inflation in the same period this year.
"It is estimated that the inflation will be 26 percent in the first six month of 1997," he told a news conference at which he unveiled 1997 economic targets.
Year-on-year wholesale inflation was 79.8 percent and consumer inflation 79.3 percent in September.
Sener said salaries of civil servants and pensioners would be raised by 30 percent in January, 1997, for the first half of 1997.
His Islamist-led government raised the salaries by an average 50 percent as part of its populist policies when it came to power in late June.
